Horace had some hope because she seemed to be amused at meeting him. He might avoid trouble if he treated her the right way. He replied, “I didn’t expect to meet one of the family.” She nodded. “I see what an inconvenience it is for you to meet me. What are you going to do?” Horace said, “My first thought was to run.” “Of course, you could do that. But I would telephone the police and tell them all about you. They’d get you at once.”

questions.stem:
He had seen the housekeeper hang the key to the kitchen door on a hook outside. He put on a pair of gloves, took the key, and opened the door. He was always careful not to leave any fingerprints. A small dog was lying in the kitchen. It stirred, made a noise, and moved its tail in a friendly way. “All right, Sherry,” Horace said as he passed. All you had to do to keep dogs quiet was to call them by their right names, and show them love.

In the passage, Horace greets the dog in the kitchen and claims that dogs are kept quiet by kindness instead of by force. What does this claim show us about Horace? (A) He believes that even a dog in the house can be won over by kindness if he treats it in the right way (B) He dislikes animals and frightens them on purpose (C) He has trained the dog to fetch the key to the kitchen door for him (D) He is afraid that the dog will lead the police to the kitchen door

answerScheme.modelAnswer: He believes that even a dog in the house can be won over by kindness if he treats it in the right way

But Horace found that the flowers were hindering him in his work. He buried his face in his handkerchief. Then he heard a voice say from the doorway, “What is it? A cold or hay fever?” Before he could think, Horace said, “Hay fever,” and found himself sneezing again. The voice went on, “You can cure it with a special treatment, you know, if you find out just what plant gives you the disease. I think you’d better see a doctor, if you’re serious about your work. I heard you from the top of the house just now.”

In the passage, the woman in the doorway says, “I heard you from the top of the house just now.” What does this remark show about her? (A) She has no idea where Horace is in the house (B) Horace has been shouting loudly enough to be heard from the street (C) She has decided to leave the house and go back upstairs (D) She has been listening to him and is now telling him that she knows he is there

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: Your colony has a shop that makes strong locks and repairs burglar alarms. Write an advertisement for this shop in about 100 words, for a handbill to be put up in the colony. Begin with a catchy heading, give two reasons why people should choose this shop, and end with a line asking readers to leave their name and address. Leave the shop's name, its address and its telephone number as blanks.

markingPoints.description: Writes a clear, catchy heading that names the service offered.
Explains what the shop makes and repairs, namely strong locks and burglar alarms.
Gives two clear reasons why readers should choose the shop.
Ends with a call to action and leaves the shop's name, address and telephone number as blanks.
Uses correct spelling, punctuation, suitable linking words and an appropriate formal tone in about 100 words.

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
STRONG LOCKS FOR SAFE HOMES
Worried about a break-in? We make strong locks and repair burglar alarms, so that a thief cannot open your door or your safe. Our skilled workers mend faulty alarms and fit new locks at your home without wasting your time. We use strong material, and our prices are fair. Do not wait for a theft to happen before you act. Leave your name and address below, or ring us today and we will call at your home.
Shop: ____________
Address: ____________
Telephone: ____________

evidence: He made locks and was successful enough at his business to have two helpers.
The burglar alarm was poorly built.

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: Your school is holding an assembly on the value of keeping promises. The Principal asks you to speak for a minute on why a person's word matters. Write your speech in about 100 words. Open with a greeting to the Principal, teachers and fellow students, give two reasons from your own life for keeping promises, and close with a short appeal.

markingPoints.description: Opens with a correct greeting to the Principal, the teachers and the students.
States the topic clearly, namely that people trust us only when we keep our promises.
Gives two reasons from the speaker's own life for keeping promises.
Ends with a short appeal to the audience and a courteous closing.
Uses clear and correct language, suitable linkers and a formal tone in about 100 words.

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
Principal, teachers and dear friends,
A promise is a promise. If we say we will do something and then do not do it, people stop trusting us, and trust is very hard to win back. I remember once promising a friend that I would help in a project, and then I let him down because of a football match. He never said anything, but I felt bad for weeks. From that day I keep every small promise. Let us promise only what we can really do, and do it. Then our words will be worth more than our marks. Thank you.

evidence: Look, I have no right to ask you for anything, but I’m desperate. Let me go and I promise never to do this kind of thing again. I really mean it.
For two days he kept his promise to the kind young lady.

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: A local newspaper has reported a rise in burglary in your area. Write a letter to the Editor of the newspaper in about 100 words, giving two simple ways in which every resident can help to protect homes from burglars, and asking the newspaper to print the letter. Leave your name and your address as blanks.

markingPoints.description: Uses the correct formal letter format, beginning with 'Dear Editor' and ending with 'Yours faithfully'.
States the subject clearly, namely how residents can protect their homes from burglars.
Gives two clear and practical precautions for the whole neighbourhood.
Makes a polite request that the letter be printed and leaves the name and address as blanks.
Uses correct grammar, spelling, punctuation and a formal tone in about 100 words.

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
Dear Editor,
Burglaries in our area have worried many families. I would like to suggest two simple steps that every resident can take. First, keep valuable jewellery and cash locked in a strong safe instead of leaving them in drawers. Second, make sure that the burglar alarm and the locks on your doors are in good working order, and never leave a window or a gate open at night. Small habits like these help the whole neighbourhood. I request you to print this letter so that more people may read it.
Yours faithfully,
(Name: ____________)
(Address: ____________)

evidence: The burglar alarm was poorly built.
There were about fifteen thousand pounds’ worth of jewels in the Grange safe.

So he robbed a safe every year. Each year he planned carefully just what he would do, stole enough to last for twelve months, and secretly bought the books he loved through an agent.

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: Your teacher asks you to explain, step by step, how the young lady who came to Shotover Grange managed to make Horace Danby open her own safe. Write your answer in about 120 words, giving the steps in order.

markingPoints.description: She does not raise the alarm but asks calmly whether he has a cold or hay fever.
She makes it clear that she heard him from the top of the house and knows he is there.
She refuses to be frightened by his threat and asks if he would hurt her, so he admits he was only trying to frighten her.
She argues that society must be protected from men like him, which frightens him into begging.
She asks whether he is afraid of prison and says she has always liked the wrong kind of people, so he takes off his gloves to please her.
She says she has forgotten the numbers to open the safe and asks him to break it; he opens it, and because she is not the real wife, nobody believes him.

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
1. She stayed calm and asked whether he had a cold or hay fever instead of calling the police.
2. She told him she had heard him from the top of the house, so he knew she knew he was there.
3. When he threatened to cut the telephone wires, she looked serious and asked if he would hurt her.
4. He admitted he was only trying to frighten her, and she said society must be protected from men like him.
5. He begged and promised never to steal again; she asked if he was afraid of prison and said she liked the wrong kind of people.
6. He took off his gloves to give her his lighter, then broke her safe and gave her the jewels, and nobody believed his story afterwards.

evidence: Society must be protected from men like you.
“I have always liked the wrong kind of people.”
Just leave it to me and you’ll have them within an hour. But I’ll have to break your safe.

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: Horace Danby planned his robbery at Shotover Grange carefully, and yet he ended up in prison. Explain, in about 120 words and in steps, where his plan went wrong.

markingPoints.description: He never cut the telephone wires, so the woman was able to threaten to telephone the police.
He took off his gloves to give her his cigarette lighter and did not put them on again.
He opened her safe without gloves, so his fingerprints were left all over the room.
He did not run away when he heard her voice from the top of the house.
He admitted that he hated the thought of prison, and she used this weakness to control him.
The woman was not the real wife of the house, so nobody believed his story and a policeman arrested him.

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
1. He studied the house for two weeks but never cut the telephone wires, so the woman was able to threaten to telephone the police.
2. He took off his gloves to give the woman his cigarette lighter, and he did not put them on again.
3. He opened her safe without gloves, so his fingerprints were left all over the room.
4. He did not run away when he heard her voice from the top of the house.
5. He told her plainly that he hated the thought of prison, and she used this to control him.
6. The woman was not the real wife of the house, so nobody believed his story and he was arrested.

evidence: Horace said, “I would, of course, cut the telephone wires first and then...,”
Horace, eager to please her and seeing that she might help him, took off his gloves and gave her his cigarette lighter.
His fingerprints, for he had opened the safe without gloves, were all over the room

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: A reader says that Horace Danby cannot be called a typical thief. Give the reasons from the story in about 120 words, and show how the ending answers the question raised by the title.

markingPoints.description: He is not greedy and steals only enough to last for twelve months.
He has a clear purpose, buying the rare, expensive books he loves, and is now the assistant librarian in the prison.
He is careful and plans ahead, studying the house for two weeks and being careful not to leave any fingerprints.
He is not violent and admits that he was only trying to frighten the woman.
He keeps his word at least for a while, keeping his promise for two days.
He trusted a stranger who was not the wife of the house, so nobody believed him and he was sent to prison.

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
1. He is not greedy: he stole only enough each year to last for twelve months.
2. He has a clear purpose: he buys the rare, expensive books he loves, and he is now the assistant librarian in the prison.
3. He is careful and plans ahead: he studied the house for two weeks and was always careful not to leave any fingerprints.
4. He is not violent: he was only trying to frighten the woman, and he asked whether she would be hurt.
5. He keeps his word, at least for a while: he kept his promise for two days.
6. The title asks about trust. He trusted a stranger who was not the wife of the house, so nobody believed him and he was sent to prison.

evidence: He was always careful not to leave any fingerprints.
Horace is now the assistant librarian in the prison.
For two days he kept his promise to the kind young lady.
